title: The $75 free-shipping threshold is paying for itself, at a cost to new customers
subtitle: Five weeks after we raised the non-member threshold from $49 to $75, basket-building and Pine+ sign-ups more than cover the lost orders. We estimate +$8.7M a year in contribution. The loss falls on first-time buyers, and that needs fixing.
summary: Raising the non-member free-shipping threshold from $49 to $75 on 2 March lifted non-member AOV by 12.6% and cut conversion by 6.8% relative to a marketplace control. Pine+ checkout sign-ups rose 23%. Net, we estimate +$8.7M a year in contribution, but new customers absorbed most of the conversion loss, and we recommend targeted fixes for them.
key_findings: Non-member AOV rose 12.6% net of trend (95% CI 10.9–14.3%). The share of orders in the $75–99 band went from 12% to 20%.
Non-member conversion fell 6.8% relative to the marketplace control (CI −9.1 to −4.5%). For new customers it fell 10.4%.
Pine+ checkout sign-ups rose 23% after seasonal adjustment, about 720 extra members a week.
The net contribution effect is +$8.7M a year (80% range +$3.9M to +$13.5M), and revenue per non-member session is up 4.9%.
